problem_text:
A network of nine research stations is positioned across a remote archipelago, with each station having precise geographic coordinates for supply drops:
Station Alpha: Coordinates (124,65)
Station Beta: Coordinates (6,133)
Station Gamma: Coordinates (170,145)
Station Delta: Coordinates (146,55)
Station Epsilon: Coordinates (58,23)
Station Zeta: Coordinates (198,160)
Station Eta: Coordinates (199,128)
Station Theta: Coordinates (178,134)
Station Iota: Coordinates (107,129)

The travel distances between stations, measured in nautical miles, are precisely known:
Alpha to Gamma: 92.3 nm
Alpha to Delta: 24.2 nm
Alpha to Epsilon: 78.2 nm
Alpha to Zeta: 120.4 nm
Alpha to Eta: 97.9 nm
Alpha to Theta: 87.6 nm
Alpha to Iota: 66.2 nm
Beta to Gamma: 164.4 nm
Beta to Delta: 160.3 nm
Beta to Epsilon: 121.7 nm
Beta to Zeta: 193.9 nm
Beta to Eta: 193.1 nm
Beta to Theta: 172.0 nm
Beta to Iota: 101.1 nm
Gamma to Delta: 93.1 nm
Gamma to Epsilon: 165.6 nm
Gamma to Zeta: 31.8 nm
Gamma to Eta: 33.6 nm
Gamma to Theta: 13.6 nm
Gamma to Iota: 65.0 nm
Delta to Epsilon: 93.6 nm
Delta to Zeta: 117.2 nm
Delta to Eta: 90.2 nm
Delta to Theta: 85.2 nm
Delta to Iota: 83.6 nm
Epsilon to Zeta: 195.9 nm
Epsilon to Eta: 175.8 nm
Epsilon to Theta: 163.5 nm
Epsilon to Iota: 116.8 nm
Zeta to Eta: 32.0 nm
Zeta to Theta: 32.8 nm
Zeta to Iota: 96.1 nm
Eta to Theta: 21.8 nm
Eta to Iota: 92.0 nm
Theta to Iota: 71.2 nm

Due to persistent adverse weather patterns, direct maritime transit between Station Alpha and Station Beta is impossible. Furthermore, logistical constraints mandate that the inspection circuit must incorporate exactly one of two critical sea lanes: either the route connecting Beta and Gamma, or the route connecting Gamma and Delta.

The objective is to determine the most fuel-efficient patrol circuit that visits every research station exactly once before returning to the point of origin.
